newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tonen plans to start Kawasaki cracker by June.
newsitem.headline: Tonen plans to start Kawasaki cracker by June.

text.p: Refiner Tonen Corp said on Friday it planned to start operation of a residual fuel cracking unit with desulphurising functions by the end of the first-half of 1996.
The 40 billion yen "H-Oil" unit will have a capacity of 25,000 bpd and is currently under construction at Tonen's 240,000 bpd Kawasaki refinery, a Tonen spokesman said.
The unit will enable Tonen to convert an annual 1.2 million kilolitres (kl) of fuel oil C into 1.1 million kl of middle distillates, he said.
Crude oil traders said Tonen is expected to cut back its use of light-gravity crudes and increase purchases of heavy crudes when the unit starts operating.
Compared with heavy crudes, light crudes tend to yield a greater amount of middle distillates but are more costly.
In recent years Japan's demand for fuel oil C, mainly used to fuel power plants and boilers, has been falling while demand for middle distillates, such as kerosene and gas oil, has been increasing.
